no-outcome.text: Created a CI gate that fails the build when a requirement has no test and no written reason, a test cites a missing or retired requirement, or a test has no tag, surfacing coverage gaps in the pull request instead of after release.

Diagnosed intermittent CI hangs in the browser test suite, tracing them to a UI test clock that stepped one frame at a time and an animation that kept re-arming itself, then fixed the test harness so a 16-run stress test went from 6 hung runs to 16 of 16 passing.

Covered failures a happy-path check misses, from missing fields and wrong types to rate limits, 5xx responses, network failures, and token leakage, making an unusable API answer fail clearly instead of writing broken data.

Audited which tests CI actually ran, using Claude Code to look for gaps, and uncovered that half the UI test suite was failing unnoticed because CI never ran it, then repaired the tests and added emulator-based UI testing to CI, closing a blind spot that let UI regression defects slip past a passing build.

Caught a traceability report understating linked tests (491 of 634) by checking the live page after release, traced it to a de-duplication step that collapsed parametrized tests sharing a title, and fixed it with a test that fails on the old counting, keeping the published coverage numbers accurate.
